_README: MACHINE-READABLE DATA MODEL — the definition scripts/record.py enforces BEFORE writing, and scripts/validate_data.py checks after. Rationale: docs/adr-011-schema-enforcement.md.
_enums_note: ENUMS ARE NOT DUPLICATED HERE. scripts/validate_data.py owns them; record.py imports that module. Restating a value list in two files is the drift this whole repo keeps fighting.

messages._note: dev #83 — declared 2026-08-14. Load-bearing for your_move.derive_channel_last_touch (joins on contacts[].contact_id), previously invisible to this file even though validate_data.py has enforced it structurally (independently, ~lines 193-252) since 2026-08-02. 'required' here is exactly what that enforcement demands UNCONDITIONALLY; it CANNOT express the anchor rule (opp_id OR channel_id, at least one) because 'required' is an AND list — see validate_data.py's own check for that. Unlike opportunities, nothing yet feeds this entry into the unknown-key guard, so 'fields' is not enforced against messages.jsonl today.

asks._note: dev #93 (public #21) - the hand-authored tail of Your Move and the Process Needs list, cut over from focus.md prose. An ask is OPEN until resolved_on is set; every view filters resolved rows out, so expulsion is structural rather than an editing habit. kind=role renders in the Your Move queue; kind=system renders in the System & tooling group. Not for anything derivable from a record: a role decision belongs on the opportunity (next_action_owner), a relationship touch on the channel (next_touch). resolves_when (dev #133 / public #22, optional) declares the exact recorded action that answers a decision ask - 'application' or 'outreach' on the linked opp_id - so record.py can resolve the ask IN THE SAME LOCKED WRITE that records the action; it requires opp_id (validate_data.py refuses one without the other, because a resolves_when that can never fire looks handled and is not). An ask without it stays on the detection path (check_action_claims.py).

commitments._note: dev #93 (public #21) - scheduled commitments, cut over from focus.md's 'This Week' prose. The This Week tab renders date >= today; meeting_check.py and watch.py reconcile calendar artifacts against ALL rows (a meeting next month is still reconciled). date may be the literal 'unresolved' - the migration marker for a commitment whose date could not be parsed - which renders as a loud defect, never silently dropped. who carries the counterparty tokens the date-collision check matches on; a date alone is not an identity.

banned_aliases._why: The SAME meaning under two spellings silently splits a query. Rationale: docs/adr-011-schema-enforcement.md.
